key_insight: The paper proposes a hardware-agnostic three-layer architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing, with a dedicated middle layer that bridges logical quantum programs and hardware execution.
engineering_relevance: It gives system designers a unified abstraction for organizing fault-tolerant quantum software, resource management, decoding, and runtime control across heterogeneous platforms.
method: Define three layers: application, fault-tolerance, and hardware.
Decompose the fault-tolerance layer into five interacting components with explicit data and control interfaces.
Trace an end-to-end execution pipeline for fault-tolerant quantum algorithms, including synthesis, correction, and adaptation.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents an architectural framework and an end-to-end example, but does not report benchmark results or quantitative experimental evaluation.
watch_item: Because it is a high-level abstract standard, practical adoption still depends on how well it maps to specific qubit hardware constraints and error-correction codes.
paper_title: A Three-Layer Architecture for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
